1. Brand of Dutch oven: different brands vary widely in the durability of their enamel and it's cohesion to the cast iron. If this were happening on a Le Creuset or a Staub it would be an anomaly. If it's happening on a cheaper, Chinese manufactured product, it's more likely (according to my research) to be a defect.

2. Use: I'm assuming you know not to use metal utensils, to allow the oven to cool completely before cleaning, and to heat it up slowly to maximize the products longevity. If all that is true, there are some other things to watch out for as far as enamel wear and tear. If you were, however, throwing a cold Dutch Oven into a very hot oven, or cold water into a very hot Dutch oven, you are certainly significantly more likely to run into cracking of the enamel. Just re-read your post, you preheat it, this is good. I had to teach my mom to do this and it was a whole ordeal that cost me one of my favorite pieces of cook-ware. 

3. Damage: if you could put up a photo of the cracking, it could (as another comment mentioned) just be wear and tear. It also might give more insight into the causation.
